\section{English-only models}
\label{app:rq13_english_only}

\noindent\begin{minipage}[t]{0.485\textwidth}
\vspace{0pt}
\paragraph{Research Question.} \emph{The K1 cells are monolingual English. If the trainings are correct they should do clearly better on the (English) benchmarks than the multilingual cells of the same size: higher scores, above chance earlier, and at least as predictable in size, as reliable in their decisions and as high in SNR. Does the ladder show that, and do the K1 numbers land where AllenAI's DataDecide puts the same English tasks?}

\paragraph{Setup.} We compare the monolingual English cells ($K = 1$) with the baseline cells of the same depth at every other language setting. These other cells give half of their tokens to English. We use seed 1904, final checkpoints and sizes 90M--1.7B, on the English accuracy tasks above chance at each size.
\end{minipage}\hfill
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.485\textwidth}
\vspace{0pt}
\begin{rqfinding}
\textbf{The English-only cells are better at English, by a small margin.} Deep K1 wins more than half of the English accuracy tasks against every other K at every drawn size (25 of 25 (size, K) cells, win share 0.60--0.79 per size, every K pooled), but the mean gap at 1.7B is 1.2 points (33 tasks, every K pooled). Shallow K1 wins 29 of 30 cells, 0.6 points at 1.7B. (Figure~\ref{fig:app_rq13_english_only}.)

\textbf{English BPB is the cleanest separation.} K1 has the lower \texttt{bpb\_dclm} in all 30 (size, K) comparisons at both depths. The deep gap is 0.049 bits per byte at 90M and shrinks to 0.028 at 1.7B (0.782 against 0.810).

\textbf{Part of the lead is beyond seed noise.} Deep K1 is ahead by more than 2 seed sd in 0.55 (175M), 0.45 (600M) and 0.45 (1B) of the (task, K) comparisons and behind by as much in 0.03--0.07.
\end{rqfinding}
\end{minipage}
